title: Make the boot-time and install-time 8-word fingerprint cover the whole signed preimage (version + secure + NS hashes) and publish the expected words per release
threat: A supply-chain or hostile-companion install whose NS image (USB router, APDU parser — the pre-setup hostile-host surface BitBox just patched) differs from the published build displays IDENTICAL boot words to the genuine release, and even for the secure image nobody publishes a value to compare against, so detection probability is zero by construction.
proposal: Change the rendered digest from `secure_hash` to `manifest_digest = SHA-256(signed_preimage)` (already computed by verify_digest and already covering version, secure_hash, nonsecure_hash) in all three places: fsbl::verify_images return value / render_fingerprint, secure measured_boot::run, and fw_update::confirm_install; keep the vendor-key words page. Pin the three to one function in sphincs_tz_bip39 and extend fsbl-tests/tests/paired_constants.rs. Process half: `make release` writes the 8 expected words (+ key words) into release.json and the public release notes, and the companion shows them next to the install prompt so the user compares device-rendered vs published words.
rationale: The vendor-signing-key-compromise review already verified this gap and ranked 'publish expected fingerprints' as one of six achievable wins: two builds differing only in the NS image display identical words today. Trezor's fingerprint is the hash of the header with signature bytes zeroed — it covers everything signed — and headertool prints it before the ceremony so auditors can compare. The on-device render in pq1 is stronger (immutable stage renders) but is currently less complete than what it verifies.
repo_evidence: fsbl/src/verify.rs:109 (`Some(actual_secure)` — NS hash verified but not returned)
docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:371-381 (verified finding + recommendation; 'detection probability is 0 today by construction')
fsbl-tests/tests/source_invariants.rs:103-134 (render-before-branch pin exists; extend, do not bypass)
vendor_precedent: Trezor core/embed/sec/image/image.c:168-176 (get_image_fingerprint over signature-zeroed header), bootloader/bootui.c:72-86 (fingerprint on install screen), headertool prints pre-ceremony fingerprint; Trezor Suite shows version/fingerprint before install. Ledger publishes firmware hashes per release.
risks: Changes the word set users have seen on bench devices (none shipped, so acceptable now, impossible later). The FSBL and secure measured_boot MUST change together or honest-row divergence (a documented tamper signal) becomes a permanent false alarm — bind with the paired-constants test. The words still change only when bytes/key change: under a stolen legitimate key they match a genuinely published malicious release (the VSKC note's explicit caveat); state this in the release notes rather than overclaiming.
